name: Checking AI Feedback Before Students See It
title: Checking AI Feedback Before Students See It
answer: AI feedback on English learners' writing can mislead, because language models may misread features of multilingual writing as errors or miss real ones, and AI detectors frequently misclassify non native English speakers' writing as machine generated. The safe approach is for a teacher to review AI feedback before students see it, at least until the teacher knows how the tool handles that student's writing. This matters because confusing feedback can cost a student confidence without teaching them anything, and a false cheating accusation is a deep injustice.

sections.body: This idea is about checking AI generated feedback on English learners' writing before it reaches the student. The problem it solves is that a language model can misread common variations in multilingual learners' writing, treating features of a home language or developing English as mistakes, or failing to catch genuine errors. A student who gets feedback like that may lose confidence and learn nothing from it. AI detectors add a sharper risk, since research has found they often misclassify writing by non native English speakers as AI generated. An English learner accused of cheating because of how they write faces a deep injustice, so the chapter treats this as a case where its earlier advice against relying on AI detection applies with special force.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, the teacher reviews AI feedback before English learners see it, at least until the teacher knows how a given tool handles that student's writing. The teacher can look over a sample of the feedback for errors and then adjust how the tool is set up. The text does not give separate steps by grade band, so the practice applies wherever English learners are writing and receiving AI feedback. The test the teacher applies is whether the feedback treats a developing writer's language respectfully and helps them grow. Feedback that confuses or discourages the student is not worth passing on.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text labels this idea with research findings rather than a single evidence grade. It states that teachers who reviewed a language model's feedback found it misread common variations in multilingual learners' writing (Barron et al., 2025). It also states that research has found AI detectors frequently misclassify writing by non native English speakers as generated by AI (Liang et al., 2023). The text adds that Chapter 6 recommended against relying on AI detection, and that this advice applies with special force to English learners.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits are that AI feedback on English learners' writing can mislead and that AI detectors are even more dangerous for these students. The risks are that a student receives confusing feedback and loses confidence without learning anything, or is accused of cheating because of how they write, which the text calls a deep injustice. The decisions that stay with a person are the teacher's: reviewing AI feedback before English learners see it, checking a sample for errors, and adjusting how the tool is set up. The text also keeps the judgment of what counts as respectful, growth helping feedback with the teacher rather than the tool.
